detail.body:
## Overview

Distribute ROCm DSA prefill indexer query rows across TP ranks and reconstruct Top-K indices with one AllReduce(MAX). Mirrored early/late stripes balance causal work without a stripe-size setting.

> Review head `2857a1e6d83e1f82cbaa2dfc8a34454c9c9ad59c` on upstream main `cd1effa2e7d204b22527f14739734751f38ed737` (AITER pin `v0.1.27`). Existing inline-review history is retained through a merge update. Supplied GPU/model results below retain their original measurement commits; they were not rerun on this integration head.

### 2026-11-03 conflict refresh

Merged current upstream main while retaining the fused CUDA MQA+top-k chunk-planning parameters and limits alongside the ROCm CP per-rank logits-budget logic. Also preserved newer upstream gfx942 prefill and CUDA decode changes. Source transport checks, 132 CPU contract and planner-parity cases, and changed-file pre-commit/mypy passed. GPU, distributed, model and performance tests were not rerun for this merge; the supplied results below remain tied to their original measurements.

### 2026-10-28 conflict refresh

Resolved the single manual conflict in the ROCm platform imports, retaining `_GCN_ARCH` together with upstream `_ON_GFX1151` and `_ON_RDNA`. All six PR-changed files are byte-identical to the rebased implementation `dd28218352`. The CP helpers and prefill branch are unchanged from `6cbb6a2f01`; upstream decode/candidate updates are preserved. Local CPU contracts (120 cases) and changed-file pre-commit/mypy passed. No new GPU, model, or performance run was performed.

## Changes

- Use one `use_cp_indexer(max_prefill_seq_len, tp_world_size, chunks, candidate_blocks)` decision: gfx950, AITER MLA enabled, longest prefill sequence at least 16,384 tokens, TP > 1, no candidate blocks, and at least one chunk with a row per rank. The builder calls it before chunking to size its logits budget; the operator supplies the actual chunks.
- Run CP and replicated prefill through the same row-range loop. Every reduced row has one writer, including tiny tails; candidate-block batches remain replicated and decode rows stay outside the collective.
- Use `cp_indexer_enabled` consistently for the operator flag. Remove the feature-specific optimization-docs section as requested in review. No feature-specific enable environment variable is added.
- Reduce the GPU matrix to two shapes at TP2/TP4 and retain only the activation, row-ownership, and logits-budget CPU contracts. The AMD CI step has two MI355 GPUs, so it runs the two TP2 cases and skips TP4; no eight-GPU job is required.

## Validation

- Local extracted-code CPU harness: **120 passed**, including the retained CPU tests, CP-disabled behavior, mixed-tail single-writer/collective control flow, tie-aware key comparison, and paged-MXFP4 budget rejection. Hardware, scorer, and collective adapters are CPU substitutes; this is not a full vLLM import, GPU, RCCL, or server run.
- Changed-file pre-commit: passed, including Ruff, mypy (Python 3.11), documentation lint, and Buildkite test tethering. Python syntax and PR diff whitespace checks passed.
- [Remote pre-commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/40636100386): the label/author-merge-count gate failed; the actual pre-commit job was skipped. This is separate from the passing local checks.
- Static transport verification: all six changed files are byte-identical to rebased implementation `dd28218352`; the two CP helpers and the operator's prefill branch retain the previous review-head definitions. The other 76 top-level operator functions retain current-main definitions.
- GPU suite command: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_rocm_aiter_indexer_m_split.py -v`. Not rerun locally because `/dev/kfd` is unavailable. The supplied test report estimates about 42 seconds of two-GPU time; it was not re-timed here.

### Essential CI coverage

- CP versus replicated Top-K through the real operator, AITER kernels, and TP collective: a 16-row chunk plus a 1-row tail, and a ragged 9001-row case with `-1` padding. Validate key count, causal bounds, uniqueness, padding, and equivalent selected scores when ties choose different keys.
- Activation: architecture, 16k boundary, TP width, candidate-block fallback, and whether any chunk has enough rows to split.
- Ownership: each query row has one owner across mirrored stripes, including ragged and sub-TP tails.
- Memory: the logits allocation of every rank fits the configured budget, including wholly replicated batches.

### Latest supplied serving and accuracy results

GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP8, 8× MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.32.0`; upstream baseline `fe5fe8ba5f` versus automatic-threshold feature `2402516767`. Prefix caching disabled, OSL 1024, concurrency 4/64. Full tables and commands are below.

| ISL | concurrency | output tok/s baseline → feature | mean TTFT ms | mean TPOT ms |
| ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 | 4 | 351.27 → 350.32 (−0.27%) | 507 → 503 | 10.90 → 10.94 |
| 4096 | 64 | 2269.79 → 2263.15 (−0.29%) | 2277 → 2215 | 25.98 → 26.12 |
| 65536 | 4 | 187.29 → 193.87 (+3.51%) | 6992 → 6504 | 14.53 → 14.29 |
| 65536 | 64 | 338.46 → 369.36 (+9.13%) | 16319 → 14534 | 173.12 → 159.03 |

| accuracy task | baseline | feature | path under the production threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K strict / flexible | 96.82% / 96.97% | 96.97% / 97.12% | CP off |
| GPQA-Diamond, 198 questions | 0.566 | 0.591 | CP off; truncation 0.374 for both |
| NIAH 65536, 500 documents | 0.990 | 0.986 | baseline without CP / feature CP on |
| NIAH 131072, 500 documents | 0.990 | 0.984 | baseline without CP / feature CP on |

The short-context workload is 4k/1k rather than the suggested example 1k/1k. These are baseline-versus-feature runs using the automatic threshold, not a forced on/off matrix on one feature revision. In particular, **GPQA with CP forced on is still unmeasured**. The NIAH feature run misses 2 and 3 more documents at 64k/128k; these results do not establish statistical non-regression. Repeat counts, raw samples, and the exact runtime AITER SHA were not supplied here. No kernel-efficiency or merge-readiness claim is made.

### Threshold and remaining review scope

The earlier [OSL256 sweep](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56944#discussion_r4344630939), baseline `bde4d00113` versus `adbd017eac`, motivates the gfx950 16k sequence-length cutoff across nine ISLs, three batch-token budgets, and concurrency 4/64. The latest report above adds OSL1024 at 4k/64k.

The [eight-query-row question](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56944#discussion_r4289987277) is answered directly: with a long enough sequence, eight rows at TP8 still give one row per rank. The sequence threshold is not a separate query-row performance cutoff. GPU/graph-capture execution on this integration head and a forced CP-on GPQA evaluation remain outstanding.

<summary>2026-10-27 automatic-threshold serving and accuracy report: full results and commands</summary>

# CP indexer on by threshold (`2402516767`): baseline vs feature

**Model:** `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, TP8 on 8x gfx950 (MI355X), ROCm image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.32.0`

| config | commit | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | `fe5fe8ba5f` | upstream main, **no** CP indexer feature |
| feature | `2402516767` | baseline + the 4 CP-indexer commits (`f395550b75`, `5f0b23bd37`, `11d690c224`, `2402516767`): the CP indexer turns on by itself on gfx950 once a batch's longest prefill reaches 16384 tokens |

The feature diff is Python-only (no `csrc` or CMake changes). These are supplied measurements on the stated commits; the exact runtime AITER SHA was not included in the report.

---

## Results

### ISL 64k / OSL 1k

| conc | tok/s base → cp | Δ | mean TTFT ms | Δ | mean TPOT ms | Δ |
| ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| 4  | 187.29 → 193.87 | **+3.51%** | 6992 → 6504   | −6.98%  | 14.53 → 14.29   | −1.71% |
| 64 | 338.46 → 369.36 | **+9.13%** | 16319 → 14534 | −10.94% | 173.12 → 159.03 | −8.14% |

The CP indexer is on here. Throughput improves by 3.5% at concurrency 4 and 9.1% at 64, with TTFT and TPOT lower at both.

### ISL 4k / OSL 1k

| conc | tok/s base → cp | Δ | mean TTFT ms | Δ | mean TPOT ms | Δ |
| ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| 4  | 351.27 → 350.32   | **−0.27%** | 507 → 503   | −0.72% | 10.90 → 10.94 | +0.32% |
| 64 | 2269.79 → 2263.15 | **−0.29%** | 2277 → 2215 | −2.70% | 25.98 → 26.12 | +0.54% |

The threshold keeps the CP indexer off at 4k. Throughput differs by less than 0.3%; repeat counts and a measured variability bound were not supplied, so this comparison does not establish a statistical non-regression bound.

---

## Correctness

**gsm8k** (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, thinking off):

| filter | baseline | CP indexer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exact_match, strict-match` | 96.82% (1277/1319) | 96.97% (1279/1319) |
| `exact_match, flexible-extract` | 96.97% (1279/1319) | 97.12% (1281/1319) |

**GPQA-Diamond** (198 questions, thinking on, 100k token cap):

| config | score | truncated_rate | stop_rate | error_rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 0.566 | 0.374 | 0.626 | 0.0 |
| CP indexer | 0.591 | 0.374 | 0.626 | 0.0 |

The report identifies GSM8K and GPQA prompts as below 16k, so these exercise the CP-off path under the production threshold. They do not validate GPQA with CP forced on.

**RULER / NIAH** (`niah_single_2`, 500 documents per length, thinking on):

| sequence length | baseline | CP indexer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 65536 | 0.990 | 0.986 |
| 131072 | 0.990 | 0.984 |

The CP indexer misses 2 and 3 more of the 500 documents, mostly empty answers.

### Eval commands

```bash
MODEL=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4
URL=http://127.0.0.1:8586

# gsm8k
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \
  --tasks gsm8k.yaml --log_samples --output_path zresult \
  --model_args "model=$MODEL,base_url=$URL/v1/chat/completions,trust_remote_code=True,eos_string=</s>,max_retries=1,num_concurrent=64,timeout=1800,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=262144" \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16384,"temperature":0,"top_p":1,"chat_template_kwargs":{"thinking":false}}'

# GPQA-Diamond
sgl-eval run gpqa --base-url "$URL/v1" --model "$MODEL" \
  --num-threads 32 --n-repeats 1 --max-tokens 100000 \
  --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=true \
  --chat-template-kwarg "think_end_token=</think>" \
  --out-dir ./gpqa

# RULER / NIAH
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args "{\"model\":\"$MODEL\",\"base_url\":\"$URL/v1/chat/completions\",\"tokenizer\":\"$MODEL\",\"trust_remote_code\":true,\"num_concurrent\":16,\"timeout\":36000,\"max_retries\":1,\"tokenized_requests\":false,\"max_length\":262144}" \
  --tasks niah_single_2 --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[65536,131072]}' \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":8192,"temperature":0,"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":true,"think_end_token":"</think>"}}' \
  --apply_chat_template --batch_size auto --seed 1234 --log_samples
```

---

## Serving the model

Environment common to both configurations:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1
```

Nothing else is set for either configuration. The baseline doesn't have the feature, and at the feature commit it turns on by itself.

The serve command is identical for both:

```bash
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --linear-backend aiter --moe-backend aiter \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --port 8586
```

---

## Client side

Run this once for each concurrency value. The number of requests scales with it: `C * 10` requests, plus `C * 2` warmup requests that are not measured. Each server also got a short warm-up load before its first measured point.

```bash
MODEL=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4
C=64          # concurrency
ISL=65536     # 4096 for the other sweep

vllm bench serve --trust-remote-code --backend openai \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8586 --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model "$MODEL" --tokenizer "$MODEL" \
  --max-concurrency $C \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len $ISL --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts $((C * 10)) --num-warmups $((C * 2)) \
  --request-rate inf --ignore-eos \
  --save-result --result-dir ./results --result-filename result.json \
  --percentile-metrics "ttft,tpot,e2el,itl" --metric-percentiles "0,75,90,99,100"
```

Sweeps run:

- ISL 4096, 65536: conc 4, 64

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Correctness of the sparse-MLA CP indexer.
+
+``rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`` normally has every TP rank score every
+prefill query row and reach the same Top-K. When ``use_cp_indexer`` says so,
+the rows are dealt across the ranks as mirrored stripes -- rank ``r`` takes
+stripe ``r`` of the first half and stripe ``tp - 1 - r`` of the second -- and
+the batch is rebuilt with an ``all_reduce(MAX)`` over a ``-1``-filled Top-K
+buffer.
+
+Run `pytest tests/distributed/test_rocm_aiter_indexer_m_split.py`.
+"""
+
+import dataclasses
+import queue
+from itertools import accumulate
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.multiprocessing as mp
+
+from vllm._aiter_ops import is_aiter_found_and_supported, rocm_aiter_ops
+from vllm.config import ParallelConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.distributed import cleanup_dist_env_and_memory
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import (
+    init_distributed_environment,
+    initialize_model_parallel,
+)
+from vllm.forward_context import set_forward_context
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port
+from vllm.utils.system_utils import update_environment_variables
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.indexer import (
+    DeepseekV32IndexerMetadata,
+    DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder,
+    DeepseekV32IndexerPrefillChunkMetadata,
+    DeepseekV32IndexerPrefillMetadata,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.ops import rocm_aiter_mla_sparse as mla_sparse
+from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import init_workspace_manager
+
+LAYER = "model.layers.0.self_attn.indexer"
+# Indexer geometry from the models that have one. index_head_dim is 128 and
+# index_topk is 2048 for both families; index_n_heads is 32 on GLM-5.2/5.3 and
+# 64 on DeepSeek V4, and it does not enter the row split, so take the smaller.
+HEAD_DIM = 128
+NUM_HEADS = 32
+TOPK_TOKENS = 2048
+# (num_tokens, context, num_chunks). The context must exceed TOPK_TOKENS by a
+# good margin, or every row keeps every key and the Top-K stops discriminating.
+SHAPES = (
+    # A split chunk and a tail with fewer rows than ranks: the tail is split
+    # too, and every row must still have one writer.
+    (17, 8192, (16, 1)),
+    # A ragged split plus rows whose window is narrower than TOPK_TOKENS, so
+    # -1 padding survives the merge.
+    (9001, 8192, 1),
+)
+
+
+def _build_inputs(num_tokens, context, num_chunks, device):
+    """Deterministic inputs, identical on every rank.
+
+    TP ranks see the same batch, so seeding identically is the real situation
+    rather than a simplification.
+    """
+    torch.manual_seed(1234)
+    fp8_dtype = current_platform.fp8_dtype()
+
+    # k_cache is [num_blocks, block_size, head_dim + 4]: block_size * head_dim
+    # fp8 values followed by block_size fp32 scales. block_size 1 keeps the
+    # gather on its NORMAL layout. Both regions must hold well-formed values --

+    stored sorted, one differing pick shifts the rest of the row. This mirrors
+    ``compare_top_k_results`` in tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -- sets
+    first, then the values behind any disagreement.

+    for selected in (cp_topk, non_cp_topk):
+        valid = selected >= 0

+        assert torch.all(
+            ~valid
+            | ((selected >= row_starts[:, None]) & (selected < row_ends[:, None]))
+        ), "key outside the causal window"
+        ordered = selected.sort(dim=1).values
+        assert not (
+            (ordered[:, 1:] == ordered[:, :-1]) & (ordered[:, 1:] >= 0)
+        ).any(), "duplicate selected keys"

+    # selected sets really differ reach the per-row inspection below.

+        (cp_topk.sort(dim=1).values != non_cp_topk.sort(dim=1).values)
+        .any(dim=1)
+        .nonzero()
+        .flatten()
+        .tolist()
+    )

+
+    for row in differing:

+        num_valid = min(cp_topk.shape[1], end - start)
+        picked_cp = cp_topk[row, :num_valid].tolist()
+        picked_non_cp = non_cp_topk[row, :num_valid].tolist()
+        set_cp, set_non_cp = set(picked_cp), set(picked_non_cp)
+        if set_cp == set_non_cp:

+        row_logits = logits[row]
+        only_cp = sorted(set_cp - set_non_cp)
+        only_non_cp = sorted(set_non_cp - set_cp)

+        ]
+        vals_non_cp = row_logits[

+        ]

+                f"{vals_cp[:5].tolist()}, non-CP-only {only_non_cp[:5]} score "
+                f"{vals_non_cp[:5].tolist()}"
+            )
+            continue

+        # Nothing left out may beat something selected.
+        unpicked = sorted(set(range(start, end)) - set_cp)
+        if unpicked:
+            worst_kept = row_logits[torch.tensor(picked_cp, device=logits.device)].min()
+            best_dropped = row_logits[

+                    f"({best_dropped.item()} > {worst_kept.item()})"

+        f"{len(failures)} of {len(differing)} differing rows are real "
+        f"mismatches:\n" + "\n".join(failures[:5])

Agreed. We ran additional `vllm bench serve` experiments on **GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP8, 8× MI355X**, comparing upstream main `bde4d00113` against the CP-indexer implementation `adbd017eac`.

The table shows **output throughput changes** across ISL, `--max-num-batched-tokens`, and concurrency:

| ISL | 8192, C=4 | 8192, C=64 | 16384, C=4 | 16384, C=64 | 32768, C=4 | 32768, C=64 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4k | −3.40% | −0.93% | +6.12% | −0.12% | +3.42% | −1.81% |
| 8k | +0.83% | −0.27% | +0.25% | +0.48% | −1.65% | +1.00% |
| 12k | −1.44% | +0.54% | −1.80% | +1.14% | +5.42% | +2.51% |
| **16k** | **+0.49%** | **+1.21%** | **+1.03%** | **+1.79%** | **+2.32%** | **+2.66%** |
| 24k | +1.55% | +2.71% | +1.47% | +3.28% | +3.81% | +4.05% |
| 32k | +2.15% | +3.29% | +3.08% | +4.75% | +4.39% | +5.69% |
| 40k | +6.08% | +5.13% | +2.46% | +5.78% | +4.25% | +5.74% |
| 50k | +4.44% | +6.38% | +5.37% | +7.14% | +5.80% | +8.00% |
| 64k | +6.37% | +8.95% | +7.62% | +9.97% | +6.33% | +10.39% |

Here, k = 1024 tokens. C is the client-side concurrency limit; some longest-input C=64 runs had fewer than 64 active requests.

**16k was the lowest tested ISL with positive throughput changes across all six configurations, also observed at every larger tested ISL.** Below 16k, results were mixed. Based on this, I propose removing `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CP_INDEXER` and using **16,384 input tokens as the initial cutoff for automatic activation** on this setup.

**1. Essential CI tests**

I reduced the real-operator GPU matrix from nine shapes at TP2/TP8 to two shapes at TP2/TP4, and removed GPU checks that separately instrumented row ownership and collective calls. Ownership and activation remain covered by the CPU contracts. The retained checks are:

- **Real operator CP versus non-CP Top-K:** a 16-row chunk plus a 1-row tail (including idle ranks), and a ragged 9001-row case with short causal windows and `-1` padding. These run the actual AITER scoring/Top-K and TP communication. We validate valid-key count, causal bounds, uniqueness, padding, and equal selected scores when ties choose different keys.
- **Activation decision:** supported architecture, 16k boundary, TP > 1, candidate-block fallback, and at least one chunk with enough rows to split.
- **Single-writer row ownership:** mirrored stripes cover every row once, including ragged and sub-TP tails. This is required for the MAX reconstruction to be sound.
- **Per-rank logits budget:** chunk sizing stays within the allocation bound, including batches that remain replicated.

The current AMD CI step has two MI355 GPUs: it executes two TP2 GPU cases and skips TP4. TP4 remains available when four GPUs are present; the GPU suite no longer requests TP8. The supplied run report estimates approximately 42 seconds on two GPUs, not re-timed here. The retained CPU matrix is 8 activation + 36 ownership + 45 budget cases.

**2. Serving performance and accuracy**

The latest supplied measurements compare upstream main `fe5fe8ba5f` against automatic-threshold implementation `2402516767`, on GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP8, 8× MI355X, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.32.0`.
